No value is resolved; all four numeric facts are review_only and the qualitative normal/preserved finding is kept as a separate included fact. Both locations call the value the median (VOR) gain of the same pre-gentamicin horizontal-canal vHIT, so by wording they are the same metric; values printed inside the Figure 4 image are pixel content only (visual.json) and are not used to reinterpret either text value.

The degree of the post-gentamicin right caloric response is worded as caloric areflexia / complete absence in the text and discussion, as markedly reduced responses in the Figure 7 caption, and as caloric weakness in Table 1. The degree is not resolved: both degree facts are review_only, while the shared finding (severe right-sided vestibular hypofunction, preserved left responses) is kept included.

Figures 1 and 2 captions say "at presentation" while the case text places the VNG in the assessment before gentamicin therapy, and Table 1 lists audiometry among the baseline testing before gentamicin; whether "presentation" means the first clinic visit or the drop-attack presentation is not stated. The VNG fact uses the text timing; the audiogram findings keep the caption time literally.

Table 1 lists continuous vertigo, spontaneous nystagmus and imbalance for the early post-treatment period (1 month), whereas the case text describes continuous vertigo and nystagmus at the time treatment was stopped and only residual dizziness with resolved typical vertigo attacks one month later. Whether the table row spans both time points is not stated; both are kept without reconciliation.

Authors state the absent right cVEMP cannot be conclusively attributed to gentamicin versus Ménière’s disease (no baseline VEMP), yet the Discussion says the right VEMP absence explains the prolonged compensation. Attribution is not asserted as a fact.

The presentation PTA values have no printed unit or time in the sentence; the pre-gentamicin baseline and follow-up PTAs (with dB HL) are recorded separately and are not merged with the initial values because the source does not state they are the same time point.

evidence.quote:
Figure 1
Pure-tone audiogram obtained at presentation. Red circles represent right-ear air-conduction thresholds, and blue crosses represent left-ear air-conduction thresholds. The dashed green line represents bone-conduction thresholds. Frequencies are displayed in kHz on the horizontal axis and hearing thresholds in dB HL on the vertical axis. The audiogram at presentation shows severe sensorineural hearing loss in the right ear and mild sensorineural hearing loss in the left ear.

Figure 2
Video nystagmography (VNG) recording obtained at presentation, demonstrating the absence of spontaneous nystagmus. The upper panel shows horizontal eye position recordings, while the lower panel shows vertical eye position recordings (degrees) over time (seconds). Red and blue tracings represent recordings from each eye. No significant spontaneous horizontal or vertical ocular drift was observed during baseline examination. Eye movements were recorded using an Interacoustics videonystagmography system (Interacoustics A/S, Denmark).

Figure 3
Monothermal caloric testing performed before intratympanic gentamicin therapy, showing preserved bilateral caloric reactivity. This baseline assessment was used as a screening evaluation of caloric responsiveness and should not be interpreted as a complete bithermal caloric test. The left panels show horizontal eye movement recordings during warm (44 °C) caloric irrigations. The right panels display the corresponding slow phase velocity (SPV) responses. Time is expressed in seconds and SPV in degrees per second (°/s). Caloric stimulation and eye movement recording were performed using an Interacoustics VNG system and caloric irrigator (Interacoustics A/S, Denmark).

Figure 4
Video head impulse testing (vHIT) of the horizontal semicircular canals performed before intratympanic gentamicin therapy demonstrated preserved and relatively symmetrical vestibulo-ocular reflex (VOR) gain bilaterally, with a median VOR gain at 60 ms of 0.73 for the right horizontal canal and 0.91 for the left horizontal canal. No significant overt or covert corrective saccades were observed, consistent with normal lateral semicircular canal function. Testing was performed using an Interacoustics vHIT system (Interacoustics A/S, Denmark).

Figure 5
Video nystagmography (VNG) recording obtained after intratympanic gentamicin therapy, demonstrating intense spontaneous left-beating horizontal nystagmus, consistent with acute right-sided vestibular hypofunction induced by treatment. The upper panel shows horizontal eye position traces, while the lower panel shows vertical eye position recordings. Red and blue tracings represent recordings from each eye. The spontaneous nystagmus persisted in the absence of visual fixation and was associated with significant post-treatment vertigo and imbalance.

Figure 6
Pure-tone audiometry performed after the second intratympanic gentamicin injection. PTA for the left ear remained stable at 19 dB HL, whereas PTA for the right ear increased from 61 dB HL before treatment to 74 dB HL after treatment, indicating a worsening of hearing thresholds in the treated ear. Red circles and connecting lines represent baseline (pre-treatment) air-conduction thresholds of the right ear, while black circles and gray connecting lines represent post-treatment right-ear air-conduction thresholds. Blue crosses and connecting lines represent baseline (pre-treatment) air-conduction thresholds of the left ear, while black crosses and gray connecting lines represent post-treatment left-ear air-conduction thresholds. Green dashed lines and bracket symbols indicate bone-conduction thresholds. Frequencies are displayed in kHz on the horizontal axis and hearing thresholds in dB HL on the vertical axis.

Figure 7
Bithermal caloric testing performed after intratympanic gentamicin therapy, demonstrating severe right-sided vestibular hypofunction, with markedly reduced caloric responses on the right side and preserved responses on the left. Residual spontaneous left-beating nystagmus was present during testing and contributed to baseline asymmetry. The left panels show horizontal eye position recordings during warm and cold irrigations, while the right panels summarize caloric response amplitudes and directional preponderance.

Figure 8
Video head impulse testing (vHIT) performed after intratympanic gentamicin therapy, demonstrating reduced vestibulo-ocular reflex (VOR) gain of the right lateral semicircular canal (median gain approximately 0.36–0.42) compared with preserved left-sided function (median gain approximately 0.73–0.80). Multiple overt corrective saccades were observed during rightward impulses, consistent with right unilateral vestibular hypofunction.

Figure 9
Pure-tone audiometry performed one year after intratympanic gentamicin therapy, demonstrating hearing thresholds comparable to those recorded before treatment. PTA for the right ear was 61 dB HL, and PTA for the left ear was 19 dB HL at follow-up. Red circles and connecting lines represent the baseline (pre-treatment) air-conduction thresholds of the right ear, while black circles and gray connecting lines represent the right-ear air-conduction thresholds recorded at the 1-year follow-up. Blue crosses and connecting lines represent baseline (pre-treatment) air-conduction thresholds of the left ear, while black crosses and gray connecting lines represent the left-ear air-conduction thresholds recorded at follow-up. Green dashed lines and bracket symbols indicate bone-conduction thresholds. Frequencies are displayed in kHz on the horizontal axis and hearing thresholds in dB HL on the vertical axis.

Figure 10
Video nystagmography (VNG) recording obtained one year after intratympanic gentamicin therapy, demonstrating a small residual spontaneous left-beating horizontal nystagmus, consistent with persistent but compensated right-sided vestibular hypofunction. Compared with the early post-treatment recordings, the amplitude and velocity of the spontaneous nystagmus were markedly reduced, suggesting partial central vestibular compensation over time. The upper panel shows horizontal eye position recordings, while the lower panel shows vertical eye position traces.

Figure 11
Cervical vestibular-evoked myogenic potential (cVEMP) testing performed one year after intratympanic gentamicin therapy. No reproducible P13–N23 waveform was identified in the right ear, consistent with right-sided saccular dysfunction. In contrast, the left ear demonstrated preserved biphasic P13–N23 responses with normal morphology and latency values.

caption_claims.text: Monothermal (warm 44 °C) caloric testing before gentamicin: preserved bilateral reactivity.

evidence.quote:

Monothermal caloric testing performed before intratympanic gentamicin therapy, showing preserved bilateral caloric reactivity. This baseline assessment was used as a screening evaluation of caloric responsiveness and should not be interpreted as a complete bithermal caloric test. The left panels show horizontal eye movement recordings during warm (44 °C) caloric irrigations. The right panels display the corresponding slow phase velocity (SPV) responses. Time is expressed in seconds and SPV in degrees per second (°/s). Caloric stimulation and eye movement recording were performed using an Interacoustics VNG system and caloric irrigator (Interacoustics A/S, Denmark).

caption_claims.text: Baseline vHIT of the horizontal canals before gentamicin with no significant corrective saccades.

evidence.quote:

Video head impulse testing (vHIT) of the horizontal semicircular canals performed before intratympanic gentamicin therapy demonstrated preserved and relatively symmetrical vestibulo-ocular reflex (VOR) gain bilaterally, with a median VOR gain at 60 ms of 0.73 for the right horizontal canal and 0.91 for the left horizontal canal. No significant overt or covert corrective saccades were observed, consistent with normal lateral semicircular canal function. Testing was performed using an Interacoustics vHIT system (Interacoustics A/S, Denmark).

caption_claims.text: VNG after gentamicin: intense spontaneous left-beating horizontal nystagmus.

evidence.quote:
Figure 5
Video nystagmography (VNG) recording obtained after intratympanic gentamicin therapy, demonstrating intense spontaneous left-beating horizontal nystagmus, consistent with acute right-sided vestibular hypofunction induced by treatment. The upper panel shows horizontal eye position traces, while the lower panel shows vertical eye position recordings. Red and blue tracings represent recordings from each eye. The spontaneous nystagmus persisted in the absence of visual fixation and was associated with significant post-treatment vertigo and imbalance.

caption_claims.text: Pure-tone audiometry after the second gentamicin injection: right PTA increased, left stable.

evidence.quote:
Figure 6
Pure-tone audiometry performed after the second intratympanic gentamicin injection. PTA for the left ear remained stable at 19 dB HL, whereas PTA for the right ear increased from 61 dB HL before treatment to 74 dB HL after treatment, indicating a worsening of hearing thresholds in the treated ear. Red circles and connecting lines represent baseline (pre-treatment) air-conduction thresholds of the right ear, while black circles and gray connecting lines represent post-treatment right-ear air-conduction thresholds. Blue crosses and connecting lines represent baseline (pre-treatment) air-conduction thresholds of the left ear, while black crosses and gray connecting lines represent post-treatment left-ear air-conduction thresholds. Green dashed lines and bracket symbols indicate bone-conduction thresholds. Frequencies are displayed in kHz on the horizontal axis and hearing thresholds in dB HL on the vertical axis.

caption_claims.text: Bithermal caloric testing after gentamicin: severe right-sided hypofunction.

evidence.quote:
Figure 7
Bithermal caloric testing performed after intratympanic gentamicin therapy, demonstrating severe right-sided vestibular hypofunction, with markedly reduced caloric responses on the right side and preserved responses on the left. Residual spontaneous left-beating nystagmus was present during testing and contributed to baseline asymmetry. The left panels show horizontal eye position recordings during warm and cold irrigations, while the right panels summarize caloric response amplitudes and directional preponderance.

caption_claims.text: vHIT after gentamicin: reduced right lateral canal gain with overt corrective saccades.

evidence.quote:
Figure 8
Video head impulse testing (vHIT) performed after intratympanic gentamicin therapy, demonstrating reduced vestibulo-ocular reflex (VOR) gain of the right lateral semicircular canal (median gain approximately 0.36–0.42) compared with preserved left-sided function (median gain approximately 0.73–0.80). Multiple overt corrective saccades were observed during rightward impulses, consistent with right unilateral vestibular hypofunction.

caption_claims.text: Pure-tone audiometry one year after gentamicin: thresholds comparable to before treatment.

evidence.quote:
Figure 9
Pure-tone audiometry performed one year after intratympanic gentamicin therapy, demonstrating hearing thresholds comparable to those recorded before treatment. PTA for the right ear was 61 dB HL, and PTA for the left ear was 19 dB HL at follow-up. Red circles and connecting lines represent the baseline (pre-treatment) air-conduction thresholds of the right ear, while black circles and gray connecting lines represent the right-ear air-conduction thresholds recorded at the 1-year follow-up. Blue crosses and connecting lines represent baseline (pre-treatment) air-conduction thresholds of the left ear, while black crosses and gray connecting lines represent the left-ear air-conduction thresholds recorded at follow-up. Green dashed lines and bracket symbols indicate bone-conduction thresholds. Frequencies are displayed in kHz on the horizontal axis and hearing thresholds in dB HL on the vertical axis.

caption_claims.text: VNG one year after gentamicin: small residual left-beating nystagmus.

evidence.quote:
Figure 10
Video nystagmography (VNG) recording obtained one year after intratympanic gentamicin therapy, demonstrating a small residual spontaneous left-beating horizontal nystagmus, consistent with persistent but compensated right-sided vestibular hypofunction. Compared with the early post-treatment recordings, the amplitude and velocity of the spontaneous nystagmus were markedly reduced, suggesting partial central vestibular compensation over time. The upper panel shows horizontal eye position recordings, while the lower panel shows vertical eye position traces.

caption_claims.text: cVEMP one year after gentamicin: no reproducible right-ear waveform, preserved left.

evidence.quote:
Figure 11
Cervical vestibular-evoked myogenic potential (cVEMP) testing performed one year after intratympanic gentamicin therapy. No reproducible P13–N23 waveform was identified in the right ear, consistent with right-sided saccular dysfunction. In contrast, the left ear demonstrated preserved biphasic P13–N23 responses with normal morphology and latency values.
